By "this decade" I'm assuming 2000 and onward.

V/H/S the first. Shitty movie overall, but the atmosphere and the idea of it are too good to not love it. When it works, it's brilliant - if you were at all into the brief found-footage online revival, at least. Some people found it overdone; I thought this, at its best, did found footage exactly the way it should have been done, delving into the impulses that make people seek out "real" found footage stuff, and the creators of that sorts of media, and the various forms it takes. Just a crazy ride along the fringes of both society and reality. Again, when it works, I love it, but it does not always work, at all.

28 Days Later, I guess? That was one of my favorite movies in high school, my friends and I watched it religiously. Dunno how well it holds up but it's got a lot of really neat stuff - great shots, classic soundtrack, and some really fantastic scenes.

I liked the remake of Funny Games, sue me. Still need to see the original, but as it's shot-for-shot the same, apparently, I'm not sure if I'm going to.

El Orfanato is a film I show to friends when I want them to feel emotionally traumatized. It has always worked. Sometimes I help it along by lying when they ask me questions about what's going on before terrible things happen. I am a very good friend.

The Devil's Backbone is quite good. It's more horror than Pan's Labyrinth, which I hesitate to recommend somewhat as it's not horror-horror. Also it's super well-known so, y'know, why bother recommending it? Anyway, yeah, Guillermo del Toro directs.

La Horde is hilarious. I think it was meant to be. Probably. Maybe. Probably not. It's kind of really bad. But it's very funny. French zombie/cop/gangster film.

Hostel the first is a much better movie than it gets credit for. It's very simplistic, light on story and character, and verges too close to having a moral sometimes, but it's unpleasant and grimy and captures a certain spark of madness that good horror ought to have without becoming too absurd, like Saw and fuckin' The Collector did. Works best when it's completely meaningless.

Speaking of Saw... Saw. You're watching horror with friends, and Saw is the quintessential "horror with friends" franchise. Because it's unwatchable without other people to watch with, frankly. Watching with friends heightens your reactions to things, from laughter to disgust to disbelief, and you'll at least get reactions from the Saw movies. If this run of horror films you're putting on is meant to showcase only the finest of horror, then leave this out; but if you're willing to do pulpy, stupid stuff, then you might as well do Saw.

Troll Hunter and Dead Snow also fit into the category of comedy-horror, with the former being a lot more laid-back and the latter being batshit insane.

Oculus was okay. A lot of really great buildup for not the best payoff.

Let The Right One In is a great film, but it might not be a "watch with others" kind of film. It could be too quiet for that.

The Babadook is good, but it has its problems. Has a bad Stephen King climax and the sound design varies from excellent (the knocking sounds, the kid's voice) to eh (the metalcore inhaled growling voice) to really bad (canned audio "scary_monster_roar_3.wav"). Definitely worth a watch, but I think it might be better for horror movie fans than for laypeople, who might not get what it does differently from other horror films or the fantastic slow twists.

That's my twenty-five cents. Tried to only talk about things I hadn't seen yet, or things that had showed up which I had more to say about. Plenty more good stuff (and bad stuff that's fun to watch) out there. Oh, and there's always August Underground's Mordum, if you want to probably lose your friends.
